newsitem.title: USA: EFTC to buy assets, supply AlliedSignal.
newsitem.headline: EFTC to buy assets, supply AlliedSignal.

text.p: EFTC Corp said Wednesday it agreed to buy certain assets of, and supply circuit board assembly services to, AlliedSignal Inc's Aerospace operations.

EFTC will purchase assets of AlliedSignal's Ft. Lauderdale Circuit Assembly Operation and Tucson Circuit Assembly Operation, and offer jobs to the AlliedSignal employees already working there, according to a press release issued by the companies.
The Ft. Lauderdale facility manufactures circuit cards used by AlliedSignal's Commercial Avionics Systems (CAS) division which makes a variety of products used in aviation.

The companies said they expect to close the Ft. Lauderdale part of the deal, including the transfer of employees, this calendar quarter. The company expects the Ft. Lauderdale operation will produce about $25 million of circuit cards annually.

The Tucson transaction will occur in two phases. In the initial phase, which is anticipated to begin in August, EFTC will offer employment to employees associated with the Tucson circuit assembly operation and provide management services. The second phase, which is expected to occur early next year, will involve the transfer and relocation of assets and employees to an independent site which EFTC will establish in the Tucson vicinity. After the second phase, EFTC expects to generate in excess of $20 million of product to AlliedSignal out of its Tucson operation.
In addition, the parties have executed a supply agreement which covers additional work at EFTC's Northwest and Rocky Mountain Operations. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
